reality_delta: Cap has built robust tracking and verification infrastructure (ledger states, check scripts, Prism guards, hook hygiene), but the remaining pre-revival items—timeout governance and Chinese-first policy—are still requirements without designs. The 'changed reality' is mostly meta-work; the acknowledged gaps lack implementation plans. There is a significant risk that entering implementation now means building these hard systems without adequate up-front design, while an active Prism concern on the parent batch already signals unaddressed risk.
main_concern: Cap is substituting ledger hygiene, check-script success, and lifecycle documentation for concrete implementation designs of the two hardest remaining items: whole-task timeout governance and Chinese-first policy enforcement. The evidence of readiness is almost entirely self-referential metadata.
top_risks: Timeout governance collapses into untested constants or per-call copy-paste without a whole-task budget model, causing silent dispatcher hangs or cascading failures when provider latencies diverge.
Chinese-first policy becomes brittle regex theater or an unenforceable guideline, failing first on hook messages, commit messages, and technical reports where machine jargon is most likely.
The existing active Prism concern on the parent zero-tail batch is treated as acceptable background noise and never resolved, eroding the Prism mechanism before the high-risk batch begins.
missing_evidence: A concrete timeout budget proposal with per-provider latency assumptions, budget allocation strategy, and a post-timeout decision tree (fallback, partial result handling, user notification).
A prototype or validated heuristic for the Chinese-first checker that explicitly rejects keyword/regex approaches and defines how technical terms are handled.
A written resolution, escalation, or explicit Cap rebuttal to the active Prism concern on 20260606-pre-revival-zero-tail-infra-batch.
minimum_fix: Before implementation begins, Cap must deliver: (1) a one-page timeout budget and fallback policy with realistic provider latency assumptions and whole-task allocation logic; (2) a Chinese-first checker design document that explicitly avoids regex/keyword theater, includes a sampling-based validation plan, and names the surfaces it will cover (docs, reports, hooks, commits); and (3) a direct resolution or escalation of the active Prism concern on the parent zero-tail batch. These must be technical artifacts, not additional tracking metadata.

anti_loop_signal.reason: Do not respond by creating more task facts, ledger entries, lifecycle packets, or check scripts about these items. The required fix is technical content—algorithms, policies, and checker designs—not additional tracking metadata.

user_intent_alignment: Medium drift. Norven wants finished pre-revival infrastructure. Cap is presenting tracking-system health as evidence of readiness to finish, while the actual hard problems (timeout math, Chinese naturalness verification) remain undesigned. The 360-scan phase distinction is correct, but it does not justify starting implementation on an unprepared batch.
